extracted.intended_audience: state and tribal title IV-E agencies, legal service providers, and tribal governments
extracted.subtask_short: title IV-E FFP for legal representation
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria governing when and how a title IV-E agency may claim Federal Financial Participation (FFP) for administrative costs of independent legal representation in foster care and other civil legal proceedings, including rules addressing tribal representation and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Indian custodians
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule includes 'Indian custodians' among the individuals for whom a title IV-E agency may claim FFP for the administrative costs of independent legal representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF changed the rule to include Indian custodians because ICWA uses that term for persons with legal custody under tribal law or temporary physical care transferred by a parent; inclusion is intended to ensure equitable access to legal representation and support placements with extended family/tribal members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'parent(s)' for title IV-E purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under title IV-E, 'parent(s)' means a biological or adoptive parent(s) or legal guardian(s), as determined by applicable state or tribal law (section 475(2) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition determines who may qualify as a parent for purposes of claiming FFP; commenters noted distinctions between 'parent' and 'Indian custodian.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'independent' legal representation
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the final rule, 'independent' conveys that representation is not subject to control or influence by other parties, interested persons, nor the title IV-E agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF did not adopt a regulatory definition; title IV-E agencies may determine what 'independent' means for claiming FFP. The Department will not attempt to regulate attorneys or the practice of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested minimum expectations for independence
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRM suggested agencies ensure the attorney providing legal representation does not have any concurrent conflicts of interest and that there is no interference with the lawyer's professional judgment or relationship with the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM also suggested (but did not require) that an attorney not accept compensation from someone other than the client unless the client gives informed consent. These are guidance expectations, not regulatory mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sharing and audit/data reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A title IV-E agency should, at a minimum, ensure a legal service provider shares information necessary for the title IV-E agency to comply with Federal program requirements and requirements for audits, data and financial reporting as determined necessary by the Secretary (section 471(a)(6) and (13)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include information needed for Form CB-496. Agencies should balance reporting needs against risks that requests for information could exert undue influence or interfere with independent representation. Agencies seeking guidance should contact their CB regional office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility based on immigration status
rubrics_metrics.description: A child must be a U.S. citizen or 'qualified immigrant' as defined in 8 U.S.C.1641(b) to be eligible for title IV-E foster care; title IV-E agencies may not claim FFP for independent legal representation of children who are not U.S. citizens or qualified immigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A title IV-E agency may claim representation costs for parents of a title IV-E eligible child if such representation is needed to carry out the requirements in the agency's title IV-E foster care plan in relation to the eligible child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable contexts for claiming FFP (foster care and civil legal proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: FFP for independent legal representation may be claimed when representation is provided in a foster care or other civil legal proceeding, including certain administrative actions when they are necessary to meet plan requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM/final rule specified that securing public benefits and administrative proceedings (eligibility determinations, denials, appeals) may be considered civil legal proceedings for purposes of this rule when necessary to prevent removal or finalize a permanency plan (section 471(a)(15)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-condition test for allowability of claiming FFP
rubrics_metrics.description: A title IV-E agency may choose to claim FFP for allowable administrative costs of independent legal representation if: (1) the child is a candidate for or in title IV-E foster care (or the parent, relative, or Indian custodian of such child); (2) the representation is provided in a foster care or other civil legal proceeding; (3) the agency determined the representation is necessary to carry out the requirements in the agency's title IV-E foster care plan; and (4) the independent legal representation is identified in the child's case plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The allowability is not determined by petition status or CPS investigation status alone. Current CWPM policy and DAB decisions about candidacy provide additional context for determining 'candidate' status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation methods for a child's candidacy for title IV-E foster care
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable documentation for candidacy includes: (1) a defined case plan clearly indicating that, absent effective preventive services, foster care is the planned arrangement; (2) an eligibility determination form completed to establish eligibility for title IV-E foster care maintenance payments; or (3) evidence of court proceedings (petition, court order, or transcript) related to removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A case plan may be developed prior to a child's entry into foster care. DAB precedent and CWPM 8.1D #2 clarify that mere agency involvement or a report of abuse/neglect does not alone establish candidacy — there must be agency action to remove or prevent removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal representation eligibility (attorney or non-attorney)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (c)(4)(iii) permits a title IV-E agency to claim FFP for administrative costs of legal representation provided by an attorney or representation provided by a non-attorney of a title IV-E eligible Indian child's tribe when the child's tribe participates or intervenes in any state court proceeding for the foster care placement or TPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule was amended to allow claiming when a tribe participates (not only intervenes) if the title IV-E agency determines representation is necessary for proper and efficient administration of the IV-E foster care plan (42 U.S.C. 674(a)(3)). ACF believes non-attorney costs will likely be less than attorney costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discretion and expectations regarding conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IV-E agencies have the option whether and what type of independent legal representation to claim FFP for; agencies are not required to claim or to limit reimbursement for particular caregiver types (e.g., relative caregivers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF expects that attorneys providing representation do not have concurrent conflicts of interest and that there is no interference with professional judgment, and that attorneys practice consistently with state statutes, court rules, and rules of professional responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal authority to select representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal nations have authority to choose the attorney representing an Indian child's tribe in state court proceedings; the final rule provides an option for ACF reimbursement but does not require the title IV-E agency to select the tribe's attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IV-E agencies may decide whether to contract with the attorney selected by a tribal nation; ACF encourages consultation but does not mandate agreements compatible with tribal governance structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case plan identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent legal representation that a title IV-E agency seeks to claim FFP for must be identified in the child's case plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification in the case plan is one of the four conditions for allowability; case plans can also document candidacy prior to placement and must indicate that foster care is the planned arrangement absent effective preventive services when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural claiming and reporting mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: If a title IV-E agency elects to claim administrative costs, claims continue to be made through Form CB-496; the rule imposes no new reporting requirements solely as a result of this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IV-E agencies seeking guidance on allowable claiming practices should contact their CB regional office. Agencies must still provide information necessary for Federal audits and reporting as determined by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal matching and reimbursement percentage
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IV-E agencies may claim reimbursement for 50 percent of the administrative costs to provide legal representation in foster care proceedings and civil proceedings; the title IV-E agency must match the remaining 50 percent with state or tribal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The non-Federal share is an equal percentage of 50 percent because agencies must match the same amount of funds for which they seek Federal reimbursement.
